sources.licence: Not checked; link and paraphrase only
sources.notes: Author Stuart Rust. Says the boat launched 'near Cherbourg in the Bay of the Seine', roughly 170 miles from Calais (the map graphic plots Cherbourg town; Sainte-Marie-du-Mont lies in the Cherbourg arrondissement, and the Premar notice and ICI/AFP place the boat west of the Baie de Seine off Utah Beach, so the article is treated as a coarser description of the same departure area, not a conflicting one). Landing at Eastney Landing, Portsmouth, by lifeboats from Bembridge and Yarmouth; a crossing 'that had already taken about 10 hours' when the diversion from Dover was decided; 625 people on 8 boats that day (Home Office); BBC Verify: average 77 people per boat in August 2026.

sources.licence: Not checked; link and paraphrase only
